items.title: 23.2.1 Structure and Reactivity of the Carbonyl Group

source_refs.note: Topic 23.2.1 with Quick Check 23.1, answered (PDF 103-104). The printed '4-methylpentan-3-one' is given its correct name, 2-methylpentan-3-one. Answers need review.

blocks.text: In the carbonyl group both carbon and oxygen are sp2 hybridised. Carbon is bonded to oxygen by a double bond and to two other groups by single bonds, and the group is flat (planar). The group is polar: oxygen, being more electronegative, carries a partial negative charge (delta-), and carbon a partial positive charge (delta+).

items: The carbonyl carbon is electrophilic because of its delta+ charge, so it can be attacked by nucleophiles.
The double bond can undergo addition, because the pi bond is easily broken; the flat shape of the group leaves the carbonyl carbon uncrowded, which also helps addition.

blocks.text: Aldehydes are more reactive than ketones for two reasons. First, in a ketone the electron-releasing (inductive) effect of two alkyl groups reduces the positive charge on the carbonyl carbon, so nucleophiles attack it less easily. Second, the two alkyl groups of a ketone get in the way of the attacking nucleophile (steric hindrance). Reactivity towards nucleophiles: methanal > other aldehydes > ketones.

blocks.explanation: CH3CH2CH(CH3)CHO; CH3CH2COCH2CH3; (CH3)2CHCH2CHO; (CH3)2CHCOCH2CH3, whose correct IUPAC name is 2-methylpentan-3-one (numbering from the other end gives the lower number).

blocks.prompt: Rank (CH3)3CCOCH3, (CH3)3CCOC(CH3)3 and (CH3)2CO in order of increasing reactivity towards nucleophiles.
blocks.explanation: (CH3)3CCOC(CH3)3 < (CH3)3CCOCH3 < (CH3)2CO: the bulkier the groups on the carbonyl carbon, the greater the steric hindrance and the lower the reactivity.

items: C=O: sp2, flat, polar (C delta+, O delta-).
Electrophilic carbon and a breakable pi bond: nucleophilic addition.
Aldehydes > ketones (inductive effect and steric hindrance).
